persons.name: Amy
persons.harm: Catfished on Plenty of Fish in 2016 by a man who extracted intimate photos and details, then posted them with her name and address and cyberstalked her for about five years: fake profiles with her nude photos, impersonation, posts to her colleagues and company, calls, voicemails and threats.
persons.perpetrator_role: a stranger she met on a dating site under a false identity

contacts.institution: Local police who came to her Denver home
contacts.when: 2016, the night of the first threats
contacts.what_was_asked: Help identifying and stopping the man who posted her nude photos, name and address and threatened her
contacts.what_institution_did: An officer listened sympathetically but said nothing could be done without the man's name and location; left a card.
contacts.quote: The police came to my home, I talked to them and explained what happened, and although the officer who came was great and listened and felt bad for the situation, given I had no idea who this person actually was or where they were located for that matter, they couldn't do anything.
contacts.what_happened_next: No investigation; Amy resigned herself to not finding him; contact resumed in 2017.
contacts.notes: Officer was sympathetic; no concrete step beyond taking the information and giving a card.

contacts.what_was_asked: Removal of the profile posting her explicit photos and personal details
contacts.what_institution_did: Nothing came of her repeated reports.
contacts.quote: I did report his profiles to plenty of fish multiple times, nothing came of it, which is extremely frustrating.
contacts.what_happened_next: She deleted the site and moved on.

contacts.what_was_asked: Federal investigation to identify and stop the cyberstalker
contacts.what_institution_did: No one contacted her after four reports; she gave up.
contacts.quote: By December of 2020, I had filed four reports to the FBI. The fourth report to the FBI was May of 2020. And at that point, I just kind of gave up.
contacts.what_happened_next: Harassment continued daily through 2020; later she phoned the Denver field office.
contacts.notes: Four separate reports grouped as one contact since the response was the same each time (no reply). Also: "I had filed four reports to the FBI. The first one was literally the day after I had heard from him in March of 2020" (s19-e2-amy-creeping-round-my-backstairs @ 20:54).

contacts.institution: Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok (social media platforms)
contacts.what_was_asked: Removal of fake profiles impersonating her and using her nude photos
contacts.what_institution_did: Platforms did not shut down the reported fake profiles; some remain up.
contacts.quote: There should be some accountability for some of these social media platforms where there were false profiles of my daughter created. We knew it. She reported it. They just seemed unwilling to cooperate
contacts.what_happened_next: Amy, her family, friends, colleagues and PR firm kept reporting; in 2024 she said the accounts are still up and she gave up pursuing takedowns.
contacts.notes: Reports were made by Amy and by third parties (friends, co-workers, PR firm); mother: "social media refuses to take them down" (s19-e3-amy-fueling-the-fear @ 22:37 in s19_02); WCN update @ 25:19: "It actually ended up being a very difficult task. It was too overwhelming for me to actually pursue."

contacts.institution: FBI Denver field office (special agent on duty)
contacts.what_was_asked: Advice and help; she was being stalked online and her IC3 reports had gone unanswered
contacts.what_institution_did: The agent listened and escalated the case to the field office's cyber crime unit; a case was opened through Denver Police in January 2021.
contacts.quote: I actually got a special agent on duty. I don't know what I said to him, but he listened to me and heard me and heard my story and escalated my case to the cyber crime unit within the FBI field office here.
contacts.what_happened_next: "As a result, a case was officially opened actually through the Denver Police Department in January of 2021."
contacts.notes: Call followed conversations with attorneys and urging by her business partner.

contacts.institution: US Attorney's office (federal review of the FBI case)
contacts.what_institution_did: Declined to take the case federally; it stayed a local Denver case.
contacts.quote: they take the case or not. And in this instance, they didn't take it. And so it became a local investigation versus a federal.
contacts.what_happened_next: Case handled by Denver Police and the Denver DA's office.
contacts.notes: Story gives no reason for the declination; the case was still pursued locally, so not coded as inaction.

contacts.institution: Denver Police Department detective (also on FBI cybercrime task force)
contacts.what_institution_did: Investigated daily with Amy, used cell tower data to obtain search warrants for Google and Verizon, and identified the man in July 2021.
contacts.quote: There was a detective assigned to my case who is with the Denver Police Department but also served on the cybercrime task force for the FBI. My detective started investigating and trying to find who this individual was that was harassing and stalking me.
contacts.what_happened_next: July 2021: "he said, we know who it is" (s19-e4-45-amy-the-mystery-was-gone @ 8:15).
contacts.notes: Father: "I can't say enough good things about how well they worked on this case" (s19-e3-amy-fueling-the-fear @ 43:25).

contacts.what_institution_did: Called her, asked how she was doing, offered resources including money for therapy, and assigned an advocate who guided her through the process.
contacts.quote: she just basically told me that there's a bunch of resources available. Everything from money for therapy, money for rehab, as well as tools and resources and an individual who'll be assigned to my case to guide me through the process.
contacts.what_happened_next: Advocates supported her through court and parole; she was reimbursed for therapy (s19-e5-55-amy-overcomer @ 50:27).

contacts.institution: Search warrant team (Denver PD with federal agents) in New Jersey
contacts.what_was_asked: Seize devices and stop the stalking
contacts.what_institution_did: Executed a search warrant and took all his devices but did not arrest him that day; per Amy's mother, the warrant shown to him bore Amy's name.
contacts.quote: Unfortunately, the agent had to walk up and give him and show him the search warrant with her name on it. He should never have known who did that.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was not arrested for about two months while forensics were done; Amy feared he would come after her or flee.
contacts.notes: Concrete step (devices seized) but no arrest that day; mother's account says the warrant disclosed Amy's identity to him (exposure), counted under harmed_by_institution_ever.

contacts.what_was_asked: Civil protection order until his arrest
contacts.what_institution_did: The clerk questioned whether she was in imminent danger; Amy and her mother describe being shamed.
contacts.quote: The clerk was standing there flipping through my pages, not sitting down, just kind of leaning over the table and she looked at me and said, you know, you have to be in imminent danger, right? I looked at her and I said, I don't know that I'm not.
contacts.what_happened_next: Outcome of this civil petition is not stated; she later had protection orders through the criminal case.
contacts.notes: Mother: "The first time she went to get a restraining order, they were derogatory towards her. They tried to shame her" (s19-e4-45-amy-the-mystery-was-gone @ 15:30).

contacts.institution: Arresting agencies (New Jersey arrest on Denver stalking case)
contacts.what_institution_did: Arrested him and charged him with class 5 felony stalking; he was extradited to Denver.
contacts.quote: He was arrested in New Jersey and when he was arrested in November of 21, he was charged with a class five felony, which was stalking.
contacts.what_happened_next: Extradited to a Denver detention center near her home.

contacts.what_institution_did: Set bond at $50,000, which he never posted; protection orders were put in place.
contacts.quote: His bond was set at $50,000. Fortunately, I'm grateful for the judge for setting it so high.
contacts.what_happened_next: "Fortunately, this man never bonded out" (s19-e4-45-amy-the-mystery-was-gone @ 25:54); "we put extra protection orders in place" (@ 24:52).

contacts.what_was_asked: Prosecution to trial; Amy refused any plea
contacts.what_institution_did: Prosecuted, but early on pressed Amy to consider a plea and warned the case could be pushed to a misdemeanor because he had no record.
contacts.quote: Very early on, there was pressure to think about what a plea bargain might look like or what I might agree to.
contacts.what_happened_next: Amy refused any plea; the defendant pleaded guilty to the felony against his lawyer's advice.
contacts.notes: Amy praised the prosecutor ("He was great"); coded acted_partly for the plea/misdemeanor pressure shown in the passage; could also be read as believed_and_acted since the felony prosecution went through.

contacts.what_institution_did: After his guilty plea, sentenced him to the Colorado maximum (four years with time served plus two years parole) and told Amy it was not her fault.
contacts.quote: He was ultimately sentenced to the maximum sentence that the state of Colorado allows, which is he got four years with time served plus two years of parole.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was jailed; parole hearings followed.
contacts.notes: Judge said her arms were tied and the punishment did not fit the crime.

contacts.what_institution_did: The parole board chair denied parole without sending it to the full board, made the hearing audio a permanent part of his file, and gave Amy his release dates.
contacts.quote: I don't typically do this or say this, but I feel like it's necessary to tell you that I am absolutely denying his parole today.
contacts.what_happened_next: He remained in prison.
contacts.notes: Audio of the hearing was played on air.

contacts.institution: Denver court (permanent protection order via the criminal case)
contacts.what_institution_did: Granted a permanent protection order barring any contact.
contacts.quote: Because I had a criminal case, I do have a permanent protection order against [perpetrator], which that was still an interesting process.
contacts.what_happened_next: Order says he is not to contact her in any capacity (wcn-presents-amy-s19-updates @ 17:53); mother says it must be renewed periodically.

contacts.what_institution_did: Parole board chair led him to accept his mandatory release date; he was not released early.
contacts.quote: I thought, wow, he's very smart and he's obviously in this role for a reason because that was a win in this parole hearing. He wasn't released early.
contacts.what_happened_next: Release expected around end of 2024; victim notification gives little notice; interstate parole to New Jersey pending.

persons.outcome_quote: It's for that reason, the only time I've ever felt safe in over five years is when he's in jail.
persons.decisive_work_quote: He mentioned the cell phone tower data was one of the catalysts of him being able to get search warrants for Google Verizon, all of the various avenues he was communicating with us on.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: About four and a half years after her first police report (2016), and nine months after her first FBI IC3 report (March 2020): her December 2020 call to the FBI field office led to a case opened in January 2021.
persons.notes: Decisive work is arguable: Amy documented everything and pressed after the IC3 reports got nowhere (four reports, then a call to the field office; refused any plea), and her sister researched him, but once the case was opened the detective did the identifying work (cell tower data, search warrants), so coded institution. Months figure is approximate (2016 month not given). harmed_by_institution_ever true because of the clerk's treatment of her protection-order petition and, per her mother, the search warrant bearing her name being shown to him. Outcome coded protected: the stalking stopped with his arrest and imprisonment, but fake profiles remain online, someone is still active on one, and his release was expected at the end of 2024. Victim notification was slower than her father's own tracking (s19-e4-45-amy-the-mystery-was-gone @ 24:52). The 100,000-page case file she obtained still contains her photos (wcn-presents-amy-s19-updates @ 8:35).

contacts.what_was_asked: Removal of fake profiles and explicit content
contacts.what_institution_did: Takedowns were hard to get.
contacts.quote: I do remember how difficult, unfortunately, it was to navigate some of the social media platforms of getting that content down.
contacts.what_happened_next: Profiles kept appearing.

contacts.institution: Denver district court (sentencing; victim impact statements)
contacts.what_was_asked: Maximum sentence; she gave a victim impact statement
contacts.what_institution_did: Heard her statement among eight and imposed the maximum sentence.
contacts.quote: He was ultimately sentenced to the maximum sentence that the state of Colorado allows, which is he got four years with time served plus two years of parole.
contacts.what_happened_next: She resubmitted statements for parole hearings.
contacts.notes: The criminal case was Amy's; Natalie's harm reached the court through her impact statement.

persons.outcome_quote: I feel safe to walk my dog without fear that he might come around the corner. I feel safe to stay at my office late without fear that he might show up.
persons.decisive_work_quote: He mentioned the cell phone tower data was one of the catalysts of him being able to get search warrants for Google Verizon, all of the various avenues he was communicating with us on.
persons.notes: Her texts and voicemails went to Amy 'from a documentation perspective' (s19-e3-amy-fueling-the-fear @ 29:48); not stated whether she reported to police herself. Protection came through Amy's case; Amy's documentation and pressing (other_victims) also contributed.

persons.harm: Wife of Amy's business partner; her PR firm handled Amy's company social media. After the stalker found out who managed the account, he attacked her and up to three of her team members personally online and went after her company and its female employees.

contacts.what_was_asked: Removal of the fake accounts and comments
contacts.what_institution_did: Accounts kept proliferating despite flags and reports.
contacts.quote: That also speaks to how the social media apps themselves have to come up with some other safeguards too, because for one person to just proliferate all of these dummy accounts at the speed and they're all being flagged and reported. Really goes to show you some of that reporting internally to those channels is a bunch of BS.
contacts.what_happened_next: Her team deleted posts and turned off comments themselves.

contacts.institution: Denver district court (sentencing; victim impact statements)
contacts.what_was_asked: Maximum sentence; she gave a statement
contacts.what_institution_did: Heard the statements and imposed the maximum sentence.
contacts.quote: He was ultimately sentenced to the maximum sentence that the state of Colorado allows, which is he got four years with time served plus two years of parole.

persons.outcome_quote: Maybe part of that is from my cathartic sense of being able to tell the story out loud, not under the fear of it happening.
persons.decisive_work_quote: He mentioned the cell phone tower data was one of the catalysts of him being able to get search warrants for Google Verizon, all of the various avenues he was communicating with us on.
persons.notes: Amy's VIS: 'Our PR firm was attacked both personally and professionally' and the business partner's wife would 'also' be heard (s19-e4-45-amy-the-mystery-was-gone @ 36:13-38:17). Her own harm is described only briefly; she still has 'a dozen or more of these old dummy requests' in her apps. Named Sarah in the show; distinct from the Sarah of episodes 6-8.

persons.name: Sarah
persons.harm: Dated a man from Tinder (2016-2018) who cheated, love-bombed, sexually coerced her, gaslit her about drinking, pinned her by the throat, elbowed and kicked her (January 2018), then stalked her (followed her, sat outside her house, watched her window, flooded her with emails) after she left.
persons.perpetrator_role: her boyfriend, an ER trauma nurse

quotes.quote: That was the moment that was like, damn, I am dating a narcissist.
Being a single mom, I didn't want to start again.

contacts.what_was_asked: Help with the relationship; she raised concern that she was dating a narcissist
contacts.what_institution_did: Dismissed her concern and made him feel nothing was wrong with him.

You can't was not a real therapist because he was like, well that's a serious allegation. You can't call someone a narcissist, which it is, but he was very good at also making [perpetrator] feel like there was nothing wrong with him.

contacts.notes: Counselor was attached to a church; could also be typed medical_or_therapy.

contacts.what_was_asked: She told him the whole story including the physical abuse
contacts.what_institution_did: Asked her what she did to deserve it; later came out to the parking lot when the boyfriend was yelling.
contacts.quote: But I told him about the abuse and I'll never forget he asked me what I did to deserve it. The therapist asked me that.
contacts.what_happened_next: She ended the relationship in the session; he followed her home and began stalking her.

contacts.institution: Missouri court (ex parte order of protection)
contacts.what_institution_did: Issued an ex parte order, served March 26, and set a hearing; the hearing was repeatedly postponed until July.
contacts.quote: I submitted the Exparte on March 23rd, and they set the hearing for April 3rd. On March 26th, the expert was served to [perpetrator] so he knew that this was actually going to happen, that I was going for the restraining order
contacts.what_happened_next: "Our hearing kept getting pushed off ... didn't get our hearing until July" (s19-e8-33-sarah-taking-your-power-back @ 21:31); he texted her on April 11 despite the order.
contacts.notes: Temporary order plus delays coded acted_partly.

contacts.institution: Missouri court (full order of protection hearing)
contacts.what_institution_did: Granted the order and made it harsher: 50 feet or straight to jail.
contacts.quote: The judge ended up not only granting the order but made the order even harsher. He couldn't come within 50 feet of me or he would go directly to jail.
contacts.what_happened_next: He and his new girlfriend ran a smear campaign about her for years.

contacts.institution: Missouri state records / courts (2007 rape conviction record)
contacts.what_institution_did: Found that his 2007 rape conviction had been lost through a misspelling, restored it to his record and put him on the sex offender registry.
contacts.quote: They were able to get it back into his record and get him
contacts.what_happened_next: He had to register; continued to give false addresses; episode notes link the registry entry.
contacts.notes: Mainly protects others; included because it arose from her case.

contacts.what_institution_did: Did not revoke the license for years after the reports; he was reported to have lost it by March 2024.
contacts.quote: His nursing license has been reported since the change in his record. It has a couple times, a couple times by myself.
contacts.what_happened_next: Update: "we have gotten word that [perpetrator] has lost his nursing license" (s19-e11-community-catch-up @ 3:21).
contacts.notes: Also "the nursing board still didn't take his nursing license away" (s19-e8-33-sarah-taking-your-power-back @ 33:08).

persons.outcome_quote: The abuse on me, the attacks, they didn't really lighten up for a few years. It was just a smear campaign all the time of me and my character, which wasn't great.
persons.decisive_work_quote: I should have blocked his email but also I think at this point it was helping build my case because he was burying himself more. I had known that I was going to seek a restraining order and all of this was just more proof of look at what he's doing.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: About five months after she first raised concerns with the church counselor (fall 2017); ex parte order March 2018, full order July 2018.
persons.notes: perpetrator_convicted is 'no' for harms to Sarah; he had a 2007 rape conviction (see P10). Delay reasons are partly interpretive: the story frames staying as codependency and not recognising the abuse rather than reasons for not reporting. The stalking stopped once the order was granted and he had a new girlfriend, but the smear campaign continued, hence partly_protected. She recorded conversations and kept emails (the host reviews the email chain on air; the apology email is read on air). Decisive work coded the_person for gathering evidence and pursuing the order herself.
